findings.location: allowlists.json roles.WORKER; scripts/seccomp_allowlists.py check_policy (execveat only for BROKER); README 'Derivation' WORKER row ('no exec') and 'Filter digests'
findings.finding: W01 W4 installs the worker filter in the child before W5, so the W5 execveat runs under the worker program, and so do the ELF loader and interpreter startup. The worker program has no execveat on either arch, and check_policy refuses one for any role except BROKER. Any filter that kills a call also kills the process, so the child is killed at W5 and the W4->W5 lifecycle cannot complete. Even with execveat added, the worker program lacks calls every process makes after exec, before CPython can run: x86_64 arch_prctl(ARCH_SET_FS) (glibc TLS_INIT_TP, glibc-2.39 sysdeps/x86_64/nptl/tls.h:154-155), and, for a dynamically linked interpreter, the ld.so access('/etc/ld.so.preload') check (glibc-2.39 elf/rtld.c:1862-1863). That check is the access syscall (21) on x86_64 and faccessat (48) on aarch64 (sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/access.c). The table has neither arch_prctl nor access. Checked with an independent merge: WORKER's effective rules contain no execveat number on x86_64 or aarch64.
findings.requiredChange: Get an owner or W01 decision, then make the data consistent. Option A: the worker program grants execveat only with flags AT_EMPTY_PATH plus the measured post-exec startup set (at least arch_prctl on x86_64, and access/faccessat if the interpreter is dynamically linked), and check_policy and the README 'no exec' wording are amended. Option B: change W4 so the worker filter is installed after exec. Add vectors that walk W4->W5->interpreter start through the worker program.

findings.location: allowlists.json roles.BROKER vs roles.WORKER; README 'Filter digests' (two-filter worker); check_policy
findings.finding: The broker's filter is inherited by the child, kept across execve, and stacked with the worker's; the kernel takes the most restrictive action (kernel/seccomp.c seccomp_run_filters, ACTION_ONLY min at :425-428). The README says this, but the data does not respect it: the worker program is not a subset of the broker program. On x86_64 the worker grants 21 calls that the broker program kills: clock_getres, dup, dup3, fstat, getcwd, getdents64, getegid, geteuid, getgid, gettimeofday, getuid, ioctl, lseek, mremap, newfstatat, poll, pread64, pselect6, readlinkat, statx, uname. On aarch64 it is the same 20 without poll. So the worker's CPython base is not in effect, and the first fstat or newfstatat kills it. W01 5.3 calls the worker filter 'the narrower worker filter', a premise the contract breaks without flagging it. check_policy and the vectors never evaluate the two programs together.
findings.requiredChange: Make the broker program a superset of everything the worker needs after W4, including F1's exec and startup set. That widens the broker, so record it as an owner/W01 decision, or redesign the lifecycle. Add a check_policy rule that every call the worker grants is also granted by the broker program, and add vectors that run both programs and take the minimum action.

findings.location: allowlists.json runtimeBases.CPYTHON_3_12 and NATIVE_STATIC ('threads: clone only as a thread'); README 'Runtime bases'
findings.finding: In glibc 2.34 and later, pthread_create calls __clone_internal, which tries clone3 first and falls back to clone only when clone3 fails with ENOSYS (glibc-2.39 nptl/pthread_create.c:297; sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/clone-internal.c:72-108; HAVE_CLONE3_WRAPPER is set for x86_64 at sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/x86_64/sysdep.h:380 and aarch64 at .../aarch64/sysdep.h:168). Under these programs clone3 is KILL_PROCESS for every role except BROKER, so the first thread a glibc-linked SERVER or WORKER (CPython) starts kills the process, and the same holds for any native role linked against glibc. The author's own research copy of the containerd v2.4.1 profile (sha256 8b012c09...) returns ENOSYS for clone3 for exactly this reason (seccomp_default.go:792-800). The README presents the 'threads' grant as sufficient without stating a libc condition.
findings.requiredChange: Get an owner/W01 decision. Either (a) add a per-call SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO(ENOSYS) action for clone3 in non-broker roles, which extends the action model, decide, compile_filter, the digest and the vectors, while W01's 'denied' still holds; or (b) state in each base a binding W03 libc requirement (no clone3 in thread creation, e.g. glibc < 2.34 or musl), and qualify the README's 'threads' claim.

findings.location: allowlists.json roles.BROKER duties (W1-W6); README 'Findings for W01 and W03'
findings.finding: Steps of W01 5.4 that the broker performs need calls the broker program does not grant, and the README does not flag them. (1) W3: 'the broker-created FD3 socketpair end' needs socketpair; it is in the table (x86_64 53, aarch64 199) but not granted. Placing that end at fd 3 probably also needs dup3, which NATIVE_STATIC lacks. (2) W5: 'The broker verified that descriptor's verity digest before W2' needs ioctl FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY (0xc0046686, the value the readiness note uses), and the broker has no ioctl at all. (3) W3: checking the child's descriptor table ('only stdio and the broker-created FD3') needs /proc/<pid>/fd enumeration (getdents64) and readlinkat or fstat, none of which the broker program grants. W01 says such a gap means the row is wrong and blocks implementation.
findings.requiredChange: Add these calls with their W3/W5 citations, conditioned where possible (socketpair to AF_UNIX/SOCK_SEQPACKET; ioctl to FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY), or record each as a W01 finding next to setgroups. Re-run the derivation of every W1-W6 step against the broker program.

findings.location: allowlists.json SERVER/OBSERVER/BROKER duty "the readers' inspection uses membarrier" (docs/alpha-2/NATIVE_QUALIFICATION_READINESS.md:121-126)
findings.finding: membarrier comes from neither a W01 row, a 5.4 step nor an owner decision, so it is the kind of addition W01 5.3 says must be raised as a row amendment, not added to the allowlist. It is also granted with no argument condition, although the cited lines limit it to QUERY(0), REGISTER_PRIVATE_EXPEDITED(16) and PRIVATE_EXPEDITED(8), flags 0, and say 'Never use global barriers'. The grant is also inconsistent: if that reader inspection runs under these filters, the same section needs calls the contract omits. fstatfs (to verify procfs, sysfs, selinuxfs and cgroup2) is not even in the table. FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY ioctl and readlinkat of /proc/<pid>/exe are needed too, and OBSERVER and BROKER also need openat and read for /sys/fs/selinux and /proc. If the inspection does not run under these filters, membarrier has no basis.
findings.requiredChange: Decide and record (owner/W01) which role runs the readiness inspection under which filter. Then derive its complete call set as a carried W01 row amendment, or drop membarrier. Either way, condition membarrier on arg0 in {0, 8, 16} and arg1 == 0.

findings.finding: S3 says containment 'labels the planeon cgroup directories' and 'pins and labels them in bpffs', and the W01 HOST_CONTAINMENT row mentions the capability 'its cgroup labelling ... steps need'. The containment program has no xattr call (setxattr, fsetxattr, lsetxattr are not in the table), and the contract does not say how labelling happens.
findings.requiredChange: State the labelling mechanism. If it is policy-based (genfscon or type transition), say so and cite it. Otherwise add fsetxattr (or setxattr) with the S3 citation.

findings.finding: Every grant and every alternative has an ALLOW vector, and each conditional syscall has a KILL vector. But only the first condition of each alternative is ever broken. No vector refuses AF_INET with a non-stream type (e.g. SOCK_DGRAM), or seccomp with flags other than 0/TSYNC (e.g. NEW_LISTENER 8). No vector allows SOCK_CLOEXEC/SOCK_NONBLOCK or TSYNC. No vector refuses clone with the thread flags plus a namespace flag, or openat with O_RDWR, O_TRUNC, O_APPEND or __O_TMPFILE. No vector uses an i386 audit arch on x86_64, or an argument with its high 32 bits set. In my campaign, 952 (role, arch, alternative, mask-bit) combinations are never tested on their own. The README states these behaviours but no vector shows them. The independent 60,000-case differential campaign covered them and agreed, so this is a coverage gap, not a correctness error.
findings.requiredChange: Add vectors that break each condition on its own, that exercise each permitted flag bit and each masked bit of the clone, openat, socket and seccomp masks, plus AUDIT_ARCH_I386 on x86_64 and high-word argument cases.

findings.location: allowlists.json socket rules (SERVER, OBSERVER, BROKER, EFFECT_GATE)
findings.finding: The protocol argument (arg2) is unconstrained, so AF_INET or AF_INET6 SOCK_STREAM with IPPROTO_SCTP (132) or IPPROTO_MPTCP (262) is allowed. The row's 'AF_INET/AF_INET6 stream' almost certainly means TCP.
findings.requiredChange: Add arg2 in {0, IPPROTO_TCP=6} to the INET alternatives, or record why other stream protocols are acceptable.

findings.finding: memfd_create is limited to exactly MFD_CLOEXEC|MFD_ALLOW_SEALING (W01 says 'limited to'; exact equality is a stricter reading, which is acceptable). In v6.12, a memfd created without MFD_EXEC or MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL is executable when vm.memfd_noexec=0, and memfd_create fails when vm.memfd_noexec=2 (mm/memfd.c:307-325). The broker's fd-unrestricted execveat(AT_EMPTY_PATH) can therefore exec a memfd, and only SELinux (entrypoint on the worker type) stops it.
findings.requiredChange: Carry to W01: consider requiring MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL and pinning vm.memfd_noexec. State that 'limited to' is read as exact equality.

findings.finding: 'Seccomp_filters: 2' for the worker (fs/proc/array.c:339 confirms the field), and the single-filter assumption for every other role, hold only if no systemd unit option installs its own seccomp filter. SystemCallArchitectures=, MemoryDenyWriteExecute=, RestrictNamespaces=, LockPersonality= and similar options each add one.
findings.requiredChange: State the expected filter count per role, and state that role units must not set options that install seccomp filters (a T04/W03 check).

findings.finding: The fd==3 conditions on sendmsg, recvmsg, sendto and recvfrom are defense in depth only. The CPython base grants read, write, readv, writev, dup, dup3 and close unconditionally, so the worker can do the same I/O on any descriptor. With no socket creation, the actual bound is the descriptor table, which the broker checks in W3.
findings.requiredChange: None required. Optionally say this in the README.

findings.finding: The mount family is complete for mutation at v6.12: mount, umount2, move_mount, open_tree, fsopen, fsconfig, fsmount, fspick, mount_setattr, pivot_root (open_tree_attr does not exist at v6.12, and umount/oldumount has no 64-bit entry). statmount (457) and listmount (458) are v6.12 mount-information calls; they are not listed and no role grants them. The module and kexec lists are complete: create_module, query_module and get_kernel_syms have no entry point in syscall_64.tbl and none on arm64.
findings.requiredChange: None. Optionally list statmount/listmount as denied for clarity.

questionAnswers.Q0: Implemented as worded, but not as workable. W02d-Q1: the worker allowlist is defined from the worker's duties, and the row amendment is carried as text. W02d-Q2: each role is its row's duty calls plus one base (CPYTHON_3_12 for SERVER and WORKER, NATIVE_STATIC for the rest), and check_policy enforces the role-to-base mapping. W02d-Q3: filter_digest is SHA-256 over struct.pack('<HBBI') per instruction, the exact 8-byte little-endian struct sock_filter layout (include/uapi/linux/filter.h:24-29). I recomputed all 14 digests and lengths independently and they match vectors.json. However, the WORKER allowlist as defined cannot survive W4/W5 (F1, F2), and the bases' thread grant does not work under glibc >= 2.34 (F3).
questionAnswers.Q1: Yes. All 123 syscall numbers and their table-line citations match my own downloads of syscall_64.tbl (ABIs common, 64) and scripts/syscall.tbl (ABIs common, 64, renameat, rlimit, memfd_secret, per arch/arm64/kernel/Makefile.syscalls) at adc21867. Both tables' sha256 match syscalls.json. poll, epoll_wait and open are correctly absent on aarch64. Constants check out against the v6.12 headers: AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64 0xC000003E and AUDIT_ARCH_AARCH64 0xC00000B7, x32 bit 0x40000000. AF_UNIX/INET/INET6 = 1/2/10; SOCK_STREAM 1, SOCK_SEQPACKET 5, type mask ~(O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK) = 0xfff7f7ff. Clone mask 0x7e030900 is THREAD|SIGHAND|VM plus NEWNS, NEWCGROUP, NEWUTS, NEWIPC, NEWUSER, NEWPID, NEWNET; CLONE_NEWTIME is correctly left out because it shares CSIGNAL for clone(). MFD 3. Open masks 0x400643 and 0x400240 come from asm-generic/fcntl.h, which arm64 overrides only for DIRECTORY, NOFOLLOW, DIRECT and LARGEFILE. AT_EMPTY_PATH 0x1000, P_PIDFD 3, SIGKILL 9 on both arches, PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS 38, SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER 1, TSYNC 1. TCGETS 0x5401, FIONBIO 0x5421, FIONCLEX 0x5450, FIOCLEX 0x5451. FS_IOC_ENABLE_VERITY = _IOW('f',133,128-byte struct) = 0x40806685. bpf commands 5, 6, 7, 8, 15, 16 match enum bpf_cmd.
questionAnswers.Q2: Mostly, with gaps. Argument positions are right on both arches (execveat flags arg4, memfd flags arg1, waitid which arg0, pidfd_send_signal sig arg1, prctl option arg0, seccomp op/flags arg0/1, ioctl cmd arg1, socket arg0/1, bpf cmd arg0, clone flags arg0). Low-32-bit sufficiency holds: every filtered parameter is int or unsigned int in its SYSCALL_DEFINE, and clone uses lower_32_bits (kernel/fork.c:2920,2924). The masks are right. Missing calls: socketpair, measure-verity ioctl and fd-table enumeration for the broker (F4); worker exec and startup calls (F1); a composition superset (F2); possibly xattr calls for containment labelling (F6). One addition has no row basis: membarrier, which is also unconditional (F5). The bases are closed sets, but they are asserted, not measured, and their thread grant fails on glibc >= 2.34 (F3). Nothing in the bases is forbidden by a row.
questionAnswers.Q3: Yes, for what it covers. check_policy refuses execve; execveat except the broker's exact AT_EMPTY_PATH grant; clone3 outside the broker; clone that is unconditional or not forced to thread flags without namespace flags; the full v6.12 mount family; setns, unshare, ptrace and process_vm_*; init/finit/delete_module; kexec_load and kexec_file_load; bpf outside {7,15,16} ({5,6,7,8,15,16} for containment) and any bpf for EFFECT_GATE, WORKER and POLICY_WRITER; worker socket and socketpair; and other memfd flags. All 10 mutations fail with exactly their stated messages, and the unmutated policy passes. The lists are complete for v6.12 (F12). It does not check the broker/worker composition (F2).
questionAnswers.Q4: Yes, the compiler is correct and the kernel would accept it. I re-implemented the bpf_check_classic and seccomp_check_filter rules: only LD|W|ABS (offsets 0, 4 and 16+8i, all < 64 and 4-aligned), ALU|AND|K, JMP|JEQ|K, JMP|JGE|K and RET|K are used; every conditional target pc+jt+1 and pc+jf+1 is < flen; the last instruction is RET|K; the length is 99-213 (<= 4096). The program order is: arch check, then x32 JGE refusal, then syscalls in ascending order, each with its own body and per-alternative skips that land on the next alternative or the final KILL. Compiling twice gives the same program. My own interpreter on all 14 programs agrees with decide, run_filter and my own independent merge-and-decide on all 1,972 vectors and on 60,000 seeded random cases, with no difference. The random cases covered wrong and i386 audit arches, x32 and negative numbers, and arguments with random high words. The digest definition is sound: it hashes the user-supplied sock_filter bytes, which are what PTRACE_SECCOMP_GET_FILTER returns as orig_prog (CAP_SYS_ADMIN only, kernel/seccomp.c:2183-2192).
questionAnswers.Q5: Every decision check gives its stated result through four evaluators, and the intents I sampled match the condition that is satisfied or broken. Every grant and every alternative is exercised with an ALLOW vector on both arches, and each conditional syscall has a KILL vector, including wrong-arch and x32 cases. Coverage of second conditions and flag bits is thin (F7). All 10 mutations produce exactly their stated message.
questionAnswers.Q6: The W6 finding is right: check_kill_permission and kill_ok_by_cred (kernel/signal.c:814-861) need a uid match or CAP_KILL, and pidfd_send_signal reaches it via kill_pid_info_type. Once the child is at the worker uid, the CAP_KILL-less uid-0 broker gets EPERM, so cgroup.kill is the effective path. The setgroups finding is right: setresgid does not touch supplementary groups. The two-filter statement is right as kernel semantics, but the contract does not apply it to its own data (F1, F2). Overclaims: the CPYTHON_3_12 description ('the closed set the CPython 3.12.14 interpreter needs at run time') is asserted without trace or source evidence and is contradicted by F3, and by F1/F2 for the worker. Also, 'clone only as a thread' as the threads grant omits the glibc clone3 path. The 'Not claimed' section is accurate.

reviewLimit: Read-only, DATA_CHECK_ONLY review on macOS. No filter was installed or run on a Linux kernel, and no role, CPython or loader trace was taken. The F1/F3 claims about post-exec startup and thread creation rest on glibc 2.39 source reading, not observation; the host libc and the CPython linkage are not stated in the predecessors. The labelling mechanism (F6) and the role that runs the readiness inspection (F5) were not resolved from the predecessors. warmSourcesAccessed=true means only that two of the author's research copies (bpf.h, containerd profile) were read after checking their sha256; all other kernel files were fetched independently.
